newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Southeast power prices steady to higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Southeast power prices steady to higher.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the southeastern U.S. were steady to higher Friday, propped up in Florida by forecasts for colder weather, sources said.
Firm, peak power prices in the northern part of the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) territory for Monday were mostly unchanged in the $14.00-15.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) in very light trading.
Firm, off-peak electricity in northern TVA was notionally assessed around $9.00.
At the Georgia/Florida border, prices for firm, peak electricity in 16 hour blocks for Monday delivery were higher in the $24.00-25.00 range, as compared with Thursday's $22.00-23.00 trading range.
Firm, off-peak power for Monday at the Ga./Fla. border was notionally assessed at $15.00-16.00.

In Florida, where most daytime highs are in the 60s and 70s Fahrenheit and lows are in the 40s and 50s, peak power prices on a 16-hour schedule for Monday were widely discussed in the $23.00-25.00 area.
Off-peak power prices in Florida hovered in the $16.00-17.00 area, traders said.
Temperatures in the Southeast are expected to remain near-normal this weekend as a cool front moves through the area. Below-normal temperatures are forecast to arrive to the region by late next week.
Separately, Virginia Power's 781 megawatt (MW) Surry 2 nuclear power unit in Gravel Neck, Va., tripped off line Friday. The company said the unit would likely restart December 21.
Southern Co's 822 MW Farley 2 nuclear power unit in Dothan, Ala., will likely return to service this weekend, the company said, after being shut October 12 for refueling and maintenance.

Also, Tampa Electric Co said two units at its coal-fired Gannon plant, with generating capacities of 200 and 245 MW would resume operating Saturday after tripping off line earlier this week to repair boiler tube leaks.
Like power prices, natural gas spot values on the Gulf Coast rose by nearly 20 cents today into the mid-to-high $3.50s per million British thermal units for the weekend.
